questions_and_answers.question_text: In the expressions vicino a and lontano da, what can vicino and lontano do?

answers.answer_text: Optionally agree in gender and number with the referent word
Change only for number, not gender
Agree only when used with people

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which pair of words is said to be interchangeable?
When is the particle ne obligatory?

answers.answer_text: In quantitative phrases where a direct object noun is referred to but not expressed

questions_and_answers.question_text: Where does ne usually appear in most cases?

answers.answer_text: At the end of the sentence

questions_and_answers.question_text: What happens to ne with infinitives?

answers.answer_text: It is attached to the infinitive after dropping the final -e
It must always stand alone before the infinitive

questions_and_answers.question_text: What does senza complimenti commonly mean when offering something?

answers.answer_text: I have no compliments to give

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which forms are usually used when referring to weather or one's activities during a time period?

answers.answer_text: Only the basic time words like giorno and sera

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which expression often means 'Thank you for ...' in Italian?
What does notte generally refer to?

answers.answer_text: The hours generally considered normal sleeping hours

questions_and_answers.question_text: Why should notte and nottata not be confused with other time expressions?

answers.answer_text: Because they refer specifically to normal sleeping hours
Because they can only be used in poetry
Because they refer only to bad weather

articles.text:
Language -Usage Notes 
1. In the expressions vicino a . .. and lontano da ... the words vicino and 
lontano optional/y agree in gender and number with their referent word. Thus: 
La casa è vicino/vicina al centro. 
La casa è lontano/lontana dal centro. 
2. The words cominciare and incominciare are interchangeable. 
3. The partic/e ne is obligatory in quantitative phrases in which a direct object 
noun is referred to but not expressed. In most cases ne precedes the main 
verb; however, it is attached to infinitives less the fina/-e. 
Thus: 
Prenda ancora un pOi di arrosto. 
Ne prenda ancora un po·. 
Abbiamo firmato due contratti. 
Ne abbiamo firmati due. (Note the agreement of 
firmati with contratti.) 
Avevo un sacco di amici. 
Ne avevo un sacco. 
Non desidero comprare scarpe. 
Non ne desidero comprare. 
(or) 
Non desidero comprarne. 
I don't care to buy any. 
4. The phrase senza complimenti is related to fare complimenti, "to stand on 
ceremony. U Often the person offering something will say senza 
complimenti or non faccia complimenti to mean udon 't stand on ceremony. U 
5. The words on the right basical/y refer to the same time as the words on the 
left. 
giorno 
mattina 
sera 
notte giornata 
mattinata 
serata 
nottata 
However, the forms in -ata are usual/y used when referring to the weather 
or to one's activities during the time in questiono Thus: 
Che bella giornata! (weather) 
È stata una serata molto piacevole. (activities) 
6. IIThank you for ... Il is often expressed by grazie di ... 
Grazie ancora delle belle rose. 
Thank you again for the beautiful roses. 
7. The word notte and its variant nottata refer to the hours general/y 
considered to be normal sleeping hours. Consequently, the following 
expressions should not be confused: 
Buonasera - Good evening. (said on arrival) 
 (or) 
Buona sera - Good night ()said on departure) 
Buonanotte - Good night. (said to wish someone a good night's sleep)
